classification.difficultyReason: Builds conditional sample spaces with repeated physical letters and coordinates overlapping at-least restrictions through disjoint multiplicity cases or complements.

content.prompt: From the letters of the word PARALLELOGRAM, four letters are chosen at random (without replacement). Find the probability that

children.label: a
children.prompt: no A’s are chosen if it is known that at least two L’s have been chosen.

answer.short:
$\frac{14}{29}$.

Count the two-L and three-L cases within the conditional sample space.
answer.worked:
There are three L’s, three A’s, two R’s and five other letters. Given at least two L’s, the selection has either two L’s or three L’s. There are ten non-L letters, of which seven are not A.

$$\begin{align*}N(\text{at least two L's})&=\binom{3}{2}\binom{10}{2}+\binom{3}{3}\binom{10}{1}\\N(\text{at least two L's})&=145.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}N(\text{no A, at least two L's})&=\binom{3}{2}\binom{7}{2}+\binom{3}{3}\binom{7}{1}\\N(\text{no A, at least two L's})&=70.\end{align*}$$

$$P(\text{no A}\mid\text{at least two L's})=\frac{70}{145}=\frac{14}{29}.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the P and exactly one L are chosen if it is known that at least one L has been chosen.

answer.short:
$\frac{108}{505}$.

Use all selections containing an L as the denominator; fix P and choose exactly one L in the numerator.
answer.worked:
Subtract selections with no L to obtain the conditional sample space. For the favourable selections, include P, choose one of the three L’s and choose two of the nine remaining non-L letters.

$$\begin{align*}N(\text{at least one L})&=\binom{13}{4}-\binom{10}{4}\\N(\text{at least one L})&=505.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}N(\text{P and exactly one L})&=\binom{3}{1}\binom{9}{2}\\N(\text{P and exactly one L})&=108.\end{align*}$$

$$P(\text{P and exactly one L}\mid\text{at least one L})=\frac{108}{505}.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: not more than one A is chosen if it is known that the P and at least one R have been chosen.

answer.short:
$\frac{47}{50}$.

Split the conditional selections into exactly one R and exactly two R’s; exclude the two-A case.
answer.worked:
Include P. If exactly one R is selected, choose it in two ways and choose two of the ten non-P, non-R letters. If both R’s are selected, choose one of those ten letters.

$$\begin{align*}N(\text{P and at least one R})&=\binom{2}{1}\binom{10}{2}+\binom{2}{2}\binom{10}{1}\\N(\text{P and at least one R})&=100.\end{align*}$$

The only excluded selections contain P, one R and two A’s.

$$\begin{align*}N(\text{at most one A, P, at least one R})&=\binom{2}{1}\left(\binom{10}{2}-\binom{3}{2}\right)+\binom{2}{2}\binom{10}{1}\\N(\text{at most one A, P, at least one R})&=94.\end{align*}$$

$$P(\text{at most one A}\mid\text{P and at least one R})=\frac{94}{100}=\frac{47}{50}.$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: at least one A is chosen if it is known that at least two L’s have been chosen.

answer.short:
$\frac{15}{29}$.

Use the complement of part (a) within the same conditional sample space.
answer.worked:
Use the complement of part (a).

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one A}\mid\text{at least two L's})&=1-\frac{14}{29}\\P(\text{at least one A}\mid\text{at least two L's})&=\frac{15}{29}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: at least one A and at least one L are chosen if it is known that an R has been chosen.

answer.short:
$\frac{27}{77}$.

Count the four cases: one each of A, L and R plus another letter, or double R, double L or double A.
answer.worked:
The conditional sample space contains every selection with at least one of the two R’s.

$$\begin{align*}N(\text{at least one R})&=\binom{13}{4}-\binom{11}{4}\\N(\text{at least one R})&=385.\end{align*}$$

A favourable selection contains A, L and R. Its fourth letter is either one of the five other letters, another R, another L or another A. Let $N_1,N_2,N_3,N_4$ count these four cases respectively.

$$\begin{align*}N_1&=\binom{5}{1}\binom{2}{1}\binom{3}{1}\binom{3}{1}=90\\N_2&=\binom{2}{2}\binom{3}{1}\binom{3}{1}=9\\N_3&=\binom{2}{1}\binom{3}{2}\binom{3}{1}=18\\N_4&=\binom{2}{1}\binom{3}{1}\binom{3}{2}=18.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one A and one L}\mid\text{at least one R})&=\frac{90+9+18+18}{385}\\P(\text{at least one A and one L}\mid\text{at least one R})&=\frac{135}{385}\\P(\text{at least one A and one L}\mid\text{at least one R})&=\frac{27}{77}.\end{align*}$$
